As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m = 2\,\mathrm{kg}$ is at rest on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of sliding friction between the object and the surface is $\mu = 0.5$. ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a rectangular block placed on a horizontal rough surface marked with diagonal lines; in the upper left, there is a force arrow labeled F pointing toward the block, with the direction obliquely rightward and downward, and the angle with the horizontal line labeled 37°. Reasoning: Given m=2 kg, g=10 m/s², so the weight mg=20 N. Force F is decomposed into Fcos37° horizontally rightward and Fsin37° vertically downward. The block has no acceleration in the vertical direction, so the support force N=mg+Fsin37°. The friction force can take a maximum of μN, with direction leftward, obstructing the tendency of rightward motion. When F=10 N, the horizontal component Fcos37°=10×0.8=8 N; the vertically downward component Fsin37°=10×0.6=6 N, so N=20+6=26 N, and the maximum friction force μN=0.5×26=13 N. Because 8 N < 13 N, the friction force can completely balance the horizontal component, and the resultant force is 0. When F=30 N, the horizontal component Fcos37°=30×0.8=24 N; the vertically downward component Fsin37°=30×0.6=18 N, so N=20+18=38 N, and the maximum friction force μN=0.5×38=19 N. Because 24 N > 19 N, the friction force cannot completely balance it, and the resultant force in the horizontal direction is 24−19=5 N; the resultant force in the vertical direction is 0, so the magnitude of the resultant force on the object is 5 N.

method.method_draft: Start by describing the image: a rectangular block rests on a horizontal rough surface, and the applied force arrow points down and to the right, making 37° with the horizontal. From the text take m=2 kg, μ=0.5, g=10 m/s², sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8, and the two values of F. Resolve F into Fcos37° horizontally rightward and Fsin37° vertically downward. Since the block has no vertical acceleration, compute N=mg+Fsin37°. The maximum friction available is μN and it acts leftward against the rightward tendency. For F=10 N, compare Fcos37°=8 N with μN=0.5(20+6)=13 N, so friction can fully balance it and the resultant force is 0. For F=30 N, compare Fcos37°=24 N with μN=0.5(20+18)=19 N, so friction cannot fully balance; the net horizontal force is 24−19=5 N and vertical forces cancel, giving resultant 5 N.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image: the push is oblique downward toward the right on a block on a horizontal rough plane. From the text gather m, μ, g, θ, and the trigonometric values. Instead of analyzing the two cases independently, derive the critical applied force needed to overcome friction. The rightward driving component is Fcosθ, while the limiting friction is μ(mg+Fsinθ) because the downward component increases the normal reaction. Set the threshold condition Fcosθ=μ(mg+Fsinθ). Thus F(cosθ−μsinθ)=μmg, so Fcrit=μmg/(cosθ−μsinθ)=0.5·20/(0.8−0.5·0.6)=10/0.5=20 N. If F≤20 N, static friction can balance the horizontal component and the resultant force is 0. If F>20 N, the net force is Fcosθ−μ(mg+Fsinθ). Therefore F=10 N gives 0, while F=30 N gives 30(0.8)−0.5(20+30·0.6)=24−19=5 N.

推理：已知 m = 2 kg，g = 10 m/s²，所以重力 mg = 20 N。斜向下的力 F 可分解为水平向右分量 Fcos37° 和竖直向下分量 Fsin37°。由于竖直向下分量会增大支持力，所以支持力 N = mg + Fsin37°。摩擦力的最大可平衡大小或滑动摩擦大小按 μN 计算，即 μ(mg + Fsin37°)。

先求刚好克服摩擦的临界力：Fcos37° = μ(mg + Fsin37°)。代入 sin37° = 0.6，cos37° = 0.8，μ = 0.5：F(0.8 - 0.5×0.6) = 0.5×20，所以 F(0.8 - 0.3) = 10，0.5F = 10，得 Fcrit = 20 N。

当 F = 10 N 时，小于 20 N，水平分力为 10×0.8 = 8 N，摩擦力能够静止平衡它，因此物体仍静止，合力大小为 0。

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, an object with mass $m = 2\,\mathrm{kg}$ is at rest on a horizontal surface. The coefficient of sliding friction between the object and the surface is $\mu = 0.5$. It is known that $\sin37^{\circ} = 0.6$ and $\cos37^{\circ} = 0.8$. Take $g = 10\,\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$. Now, a force $F$ is applied to the object at an angle $\theta = 37^{\circ}$ below the horizontal.

1. When $F=10\mathrm{N}$, find the magnitude of the resultant force on the object.
2. When $F=30\mathrm{N}$, find the magnitude of the resultant force on the object.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a rectangular block placed on a horizontal rough surface marked with diagonal lines; in the upper left, there is a force arrow labeled F pointing toward the block, with the direction obliquely rightward and downward, and the angle with the horizontal line labeled 37°. Reasoning: Given m=2 kg, g=10 m/s², so the weight mg=20 N. Force F is decomposed into Fcos37° horizontally rightward and Fsin37° vertically downward. The block has no acceleration in the vertical direction, so the support force N=mg+Fsin37°. The friction force can take a maximum of μN, with direction leftward, obstructing the tendency of rightward motion. When F=10 N, the horizontal component Fcos37°=10×0.8=8 N; the vertically downward component Fsin37°=10×0.6=6 N, so N=20+6=26 N, and the maximum friction force μN=0.5×26=13 N. Because 8 N < 13 N, the friction force can completely balance the horizontal component, and the resultant force is 0. When F=30 N, the horizontal component Fcos37°=30×0.8=24 N; the vertically downward component Fsin37°=30×0.6=18 N, so N=20+18=38 N, and the maximum friction force μN=0.5×38=19 N. Because 24 N > 19 N, the friction force cannot completely balance it, and the resultant force in the horizontal direction is 24−19=5 N; the resultant force in the vertical direction is 0, so the magnitude of the resultant force on the object is 5 N.
